question:
A 38-year-old student in medical school seeks care at the student health facility due to sleep difficulties.
Despite his academic success, he has developed an increasing fear of academic failure over recent
months. He reports waking up 10-15 times nightly to verify information in his textbooks. These thoughts
and behaviors persist despite his attempts to control them, resulting in significant anxiety and sleep
deprivation. His medical history is unremarkable, though there is a family history of Tourette's
syndrome in a parent. The patient begins cognitive behavioral therapy and is prescribed a first-line
medication for his condition. After eight weeks, the medication shows no effectiveness. Which
medication would be most appropriate to add to his current treatment plan? Answer Choices: (A)
Clonazepam (B) Buspirone (C) Sertraline (D) Aripiprazole (E) Olanzapine (F) Propranolol (G)
Risperidone (H) Ziprasidone (I) Haloperidol (J) Quetiapine
 A. Ziprasidone
B. Sertraline
C. Risperidone
D. Propranolol
E. Quetiapine
F. Buspirone
G. Olanzapine
H. Haloperidol
I. Clonazepam
J. Aripiprazole
